messages:
olivia: FYI ran a short perf sweep on host ingress after the kernel selector change. p95 for short chats jumped ~30ms

raj: short chats = <100 tokens?

olivia: yep. p50 flat. flame shows two hotspots: tokenizer.emit_frame -> many small writev calls, and syscall:sendmsg bursts

emma: did we accidentally remove MSG_MORE somewhere in the new parser sink? that would force TCP pushes per write

kai: I grep'd the change and saw a refactor that split the sink; looks like MSG_MORE flag wasn't propagated into the new path

olivia: tcpdump also shows lots of 600B DATA frames + HTTP2 WINDOW_UPDATE noise

raj: and kvcache metrics? any unexpected puts/evictions?

olivia: kv.put_rate up 2x during spike window, hit_rate down a few pct. trace link: http://perf.internal/trace/616543

emma: so two cooperating problems: early flush in preparse (control tokens) creating transient kvcache entries, and missing MSG_MORE leading to socket-level fragmentation

kai: quick fixes: 1) restore MSG_MORE in tokenizer sink; 2) revert early prefix flush behavior; 3) add autobatcher opt-in hold window when arrival_rate high

raj: autobatcher hold needs feature flag. we can't increase p50 for everyone. make it conditional on client.realtime=false or small-emit-cost estimate

olivia: agreed. I'll open the revert PR and a small MSG_MORE patch. canary deploy planned after CI

ops-bot: deploy requested by olivia to canary-4 queued (run: dpl-616543) :rocket:

emma: also propose: add per-prefix ephemeral TTL for parser-inserted KV entries to limit churn until we fix preparse logic

kai: and kernel-selector tweak: if expected_coalesce_batch >=2 and seq_len<64 prefer default kernel to keep batch alignment and reduce microbatching

raj: nice triage. once canary is up, run a 2h soak with short-chat workload and capture tcpdump + flame + kv metrics

olivia: will do. I'll post results here and tag folks. thanks! :thumbsup:
